title_zh: DIW-Printed Biomass-Based Radiative Coolers with Phase Change for Extended Thermoelectric Output
title_en: DIW-Printed Biomass-Based Radiative Coolers with Phase Change for Extended Thermoelectric Output
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Abstract Radiative cooling offers a low-energy route for thermal management, but conventional coolers are difficult to match with fluctuating heat loads and suffer from nighttime overcooling. Hence, dynamic radiative coolers were developed through direct ink writing (DIW) of a composite gel ink (MH) comprising thermally treated cellulose nanocrystals (HTCNCs) and a microencapsulated phase change material (MEPCM). A simple thermal treatment converts a low-concentration cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) suspension into a self-supporting HTCNCs gel through localized hydrolysis, promoting the formation of a hydrogen-bonded network. The HTCNCs scaffold provides structural support and mid-infrared emission, whereas MEPCM introduces latent heat storage and release. Accordingly, DIW-printed MH exhibits an average solar reflectance of 96.8% and an average emissivity of 87.0%. Outdoor tests show that the DIW-printed MH cooler lowers the daytime temperature by 2.5 °C and suppresses overcooling at night. When integrated with a thermoelectric generator (TEG), DIW-printed MH effectively extends the duration of the temperature difference between the hot and cold ends. This study provides a strategy for designing dynamic radiative cooling materials and sustainable thermoelectric power generation systems.

title_zh: Cooling Milk Without Power: The Night-Sky and Evaporation Bound for an Evening Milking
title_en: Cooling Milk Without Power: The Night-Sky and Evaporation Bound for an Evening Milking
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Evening milk on small farms often has to wait until a morning collection, and without refrigeration it spoils during the night. This paper computes what two passive methods, and their combination, can actually do for a stated case: 20 L of milk at 37 C, held for 10 hours overnight. The methods are night-sky radiative cooling from a shallow 1.0 m2 pan, evaporative cooling of a cloth-wrapped can, and a combined design (the pan plus a wetted cloth skirt). Five night climates are considered, from a cool clear highland (night-mean 12 C) to a hot humid overcast night (30 C, 90 % relative humidity). A stated bacterial growth model is integrated along each computed temperature history. Only one combination of method and climate reaches the 4 C refrigeration target: the radiative pan alone on the cool clear highland night, reaching 3.8 C after 10 h and crossing 4 C at 8.7 h. In an arid clear night (22 C, 30 % relative humidity) the combined design brings 20 L to 11.8 C and holds the modelled bacterial count to 8.29e4 CFU/mL, against 5.53e7 CFU/mL for an uncooled can. In hot humid nights passive cooling fails outright: under a hot humid, partly cloudy night (28 C, 85 % relative humidity) every method, including the combination, exceeds a 1e6 CFU/mL comparison threshold within 10 h, so in those climates the milk must be processed the same evening, by fermentation or by heating, rather than stored as liquid milk. title_zh: Passive Cooling for Medicine Storage in a Hot Clinic Without Reliable Power: A Radiative, Evaporative and Thermal-Mass Cabinet Design and Its Computed Climate Envelope
title_en: Passive Cooling for Medicine Storage in a Hot Clinic Without Reliable Power: A Radiative, Evaporative and Thermal-Mass Cabinet Design and Its Computed Climate Envelope
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Design study for a passive drug cabinet for a hot clinic with no reliable power, combining night-sky radiative cooling, an indirect evaporative jacket, an 80 kg water thermal store and 100 mm polyurethane insulation. A lumped thermal model integrated over 48 hours finds the cabinet holds at or below 25 C on a 40 C peak, 20% daytime humidity day (maximum 24.95 C radiative only, 23.84 C with evaporation). A sweep of 48 climate combinations (peaks 32-45 C, humidity 10-80%) finds 23 combinations hold on radiative cooling alone, 3 hold only with the evaporative stage, and 22 fail, including all 45 C peaks and humid 40 C conditions. Parts cost is estimated at 670 USD. All results are simulated, not measured.

title_zh: The Passive Radiative Cooling Ceiling, Recomputed: Planck-Spectrum Integrals for Selective and Blackbody Emitters at Three Water-Vapour Loadings
title_en: The Passive Radiative Cooling Ceiling, Recomputed: Planck-Spectrum Integrals for Selective and Blackbody Emitters at Three Water-Vapour Loadings
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: A surface facing a clear sky radiates through the 8-13 micrometre atmospheric window and can cool below ambient. From numerical Planck-spectrum integrals with a stated band-averaged atmospheric transmittance model (zenith window transmittance 0.85, 0.65, 0.40 at precipitable water vapour 5, 15, 30 mm), the net night-time cooling power at 300 K is 110.8, 72.7 and 36.4 W/m2, identical for an ideal selective emitter and an ideal blackbody. Maximum drops with no non-radiative transfer are 68.7, 37.8 and 17.0 K (selective) against 20.0, 12.7 and 6.1 K (blackbody). Comparison with published experiments shows exposed-surface powers are already near the dry-sky ceiling, and remaining headroom lies in suppressing non-radiative and solar parasitic gains.

title_zh: Climate-Responsive Data Centre Envelope Performance Under Contrasting Nepalese Climates
title_en: Climate-Responsive Data Centre Envelope Performance Under Contrasting Nepalese Climates
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Data-centre cooling demand is dominated by continuous internal information technology (IT) heat generation, yet the effectiveness of envelope strategies across contrasting climates and IT-load intensities remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluates twelve envelope and architectural scenarios for a 300 m² data-centre prototype under three contrasting climates using OpenStudio and EnergyPlus, complemented by IT-load sensitivity analysis and independent one-dimensional transient heat-transfer cross-verification. At 500 W/m², the combined reflective roof-and-wall case achieved annual cooling-demand reductions of 2.70–4.72%, while the passive radiative cooling-air-layer configuration produced the largest peak reductions of 7.20–11.57%. Insulation performance varied markedly with climate, and annual cooling demand increased under some cooler conditions. As IT-load density increased, relative envelope savings declined, whereas absolute annual savings remained comparatively stable. The findings show that data-centre envelope performance should be evaluated by considering the combined effects of climate, internal heat intensity, and annual versus peak cooling objectives to support climate-responsive and performance-based envelope design.

title_zh: Experimental outdoor evaluation of adaptive radiative cooling and a dew-relocating shutter for renewable-energy photovoltaic systems
title_en: Experimental outdoor evaluation of adaptive radiative cooling and a dew-relocating shutter for renewable-energy photovoltaic systems

abstract_en: Daytime radiative cooling can reduce photovoltaic (PV) operating temperatures but may intensify nocturnal overcooling, dew formation, and dust adhesion. This study experimentally evaluated a transparent polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) radiative-cooling film integrated with an adaptive low-emissivity shutter under hot-arid outdoor conditions in Najran, Saudi Arabia. Eight 100-W monocrystalline PERC modules were investigated using a replicated 2 × 2 factorial design comprising bare (PV-B), film-only (PV-RC), shutter-only (PV-AS), and integrated (PV-AD) configurations. The PDMS film exhibited a solar-weighted transmittance of 0.914 and an atmospheric-window emissivity of 0.918, with a 2.09% optical power penalty. Film presence reduced the adjusted peak-period front-glass temperature by 4.24 °C, although the associated cooling gain did not fully offset optical attenuation under clean conditions. The optimized shutter configuration employed a 30-mm gap, a 1.55 °C activation threshold, and a 1.08 °C hysteresis width. Adaptive shielding reduced PV-surface Dew Exposure Index by 74.9%, wetness duration by 75.7%, and dew mass by 83.8%, primarily relocating condensation to the externally drained shutter surface. Shutter actuation required 0.40 Wh night −1 , with controller and sensor consumption accounted for separately. Despite a 0.33% clean-condition net-energy deficit, PV-AD achieved a day-45 soiling ratio of 0.955 compared with 0.896 for PV-B. title_zh: Hierarchically Porous PDMS/ZIF-8@h-BN Bilayer Composite Membrane Enabling Synergistic Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling and Efficient Thermal Conduction for Electronic Thermal Management
title_en: Hierarchically Porous PDMS/ZIF-8@h-BN Bilayer Composite Membrane Enabling Synergistic Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling and Efficient Thermal Conduction for Electronic Thermal Management
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: The advancement of 5G and emerging 6G communications drives the integration and miniaturization of outdoor electronics, triggering an exponential surge in chip heat flux and severe challenges for low-energy passive thermal management. Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) has emerged as a novel zero-energy cooling technology. Herein, a bilayer PDRC composite (B-PDRC) integrating radiative cooling and in-plane thermal conduction is designed and fabricated. The top radiative cooling layer is a hierarchically porous Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)/zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) foam prepared via a template-sacrificial method combined with vacuum impregnation, while the bottom thermally conductive layer is a PDMS/hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) dense film fabricated by solution casting. The multiscale scattering induced by micron-sized pores and 600-800 nm ZIF-8 nanoparticles delivers a high solar reflectance of 94.45%, and the C-N bonds of ZIF-8 boost the average atmospheric window emissivity to 93.22%, compensating for the emissivity valley of neat PDMS. The h-BN fillers construct continuous thermal conduction paths, elevating the in-plane thermal conductivity to 0.92 W m-1 K-1 at 20 wt % of h-BN, a 179% enhancement compared to neat PDMS. Indoor tests demonstrate a maximum temperature drop of 11.9 °C for a charging smartphone covered with B-PDRC. Outdoor measurements under sunny conditions achieve a maximum subambient cooling of 8.8 °C, and a 14.8 °C temperature reduction for an operating smartphone. title_zh: Impact‐Tolerant Radiative Cooling Enabled by Bioinspired Multiscale Glass Composite Coatings
title_en: Impact‐Tolerant Radiative Cooling Enabled by Bioinspired Multiscale Glass Composite Coatings
authors_short: Zhixiong Wen；Jiaming Zhong；Li Ping Hao 等
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Passive radiative cooling coatings are commonly designed for high reflectance under undamaged conditions, whereas protective surfaces must retain their optical function during impact. Reconciling mechanical and optical properties in a single material has been a challenge. The glass sponge ( Euplectella sp .) maintains damage tolerance with desirable optical properties by laminated nanocomposite designs. Inspiring from this hierarchical structure, a rapidly photocurable polyurethane acrylate/Glass (PUA/Glass) multilayer composite coating is developed to confine impact damage while preserving radiative cooling performance. Alternating compliant PUA interlayers deflect and arrest cracks, whereas hollow glass microspheres (HGMs) and TiO 2 /Al 2 O 3 nanoparticles in glass layers redistribute load across multiple scales. HGM crushing, shell fragmentation, and local particle‐matrix debonding dissipate energy yet retain or reconstruct air/glass/polymer interfaces; by contrast, connected macroscopic cracks disrupt the reflective layer. The coating combines solar reflectance above 92% with atmospheric‐window emittance above 95% and remains, on average, 10.42°C below ambient during daytime outdoor testing. After a 20 J impact, localized hierarchical pores preserve reflectance and local cooling, while repeated 1 J impacts reveal a transition from optically tolerable microscale damage to reflectance‐degrading macrocracks. These results provide a route toward impact‐tolerant radiative‐cooling surfaces for protective components.

title_zh: A Bioinspired Photon‐Gated Phase‐Change Textile for Two‐Stage Heat‐Flux Regulation of Building Envelopes
title_en: A Bioinspired Photon‐Gated Phase‐Change Textile for Two‐Stage Heat‐Flux Regulation of Building Envelopes
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Passive cooling textiles for buildings must do more than reflect sunlight; they must also buffer transient heat under real outdoor conditions. Here we report a continuous coaxial wet‐spinning strategy for fabricating a microencapsulated phase‐change material (mPCM)‐integrated radiative‐cooling meta‐fabric (MFRP), consisting of a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU)/hexagonal boron nitride (h‐BN)/barium sulfate (BaSO 4 ) photon‐regulating sheath and a TPU/mPCM latent‐heat core. The spatially separated architecture integrates broadband solar reflection, atmospheric‐window emission, and phase‐change thermal buffering within one fiber platform. The optimized meta‐fabric shows high solar reflectance (95.44%), strong atmospheric‐window emissivity (96.21%), and a melting enthalpy of 102.28 J/g. In a representative sunny‐day test, MFRP reduced the chamber temperature by up to 10.36°C relative to the blank control; three‐day cement‐panel measurements further yielded an average peak‐temperature reduction of 7.51°C ± 2.17°C relative to bare cement. Energy‐balance analysis and climate‐scale modelling further indicate promising cooling‐energy and carbon‐reduction potential in hot and cooling‐dominated regions. These results establish wet‐spun radiative cooling/phase‐change material meta‐fabrics as continuously processable exterior textile candidates for passive building thermal management.

title_zh: Responses of surface radiative balance to wildfires differ across ecosystems
title_en: Responses of surface radiative balance to wildfires differ across ecosystems
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Wildfires alter land surface albedo and temperature, modulating the radiative budget and climate. Previous studies have predominantly reported enhanced shortwave absorption induced by post-fire surface darkening over forests. Here, using two-decade (2001–2020) satellite observations of wildfires, we show that post-fire summer surface albedo and radiative balance shifts vary significantly across ecosystems. Broadleaf forests and grasslands exhibit a brightening effect, because the exposure of bright soils and rapid vegetation regrowth outweigh the deposition of dark carbonaceous residues. The post-fire surface brightening then amplifies the warming-driven radiative cooling. Conversely, in needleleaf forests, shrublands, and savannas, post-fire surface darkening increases shortwave absorption, yet warming-driven longwave radiative losses remain dominant, leading to net radiative cooling. Surface radiative fluxes exhibit high sensitivity to fire size in mid-to-high latitude regions driven by distinct fire-ecosystem feedbacks. Therefore, the ecosystem heterogeneity must be considered when assessing the effects of wildfires on the surface radiative budget and climate.

title_zh: Bio‐Inspired Rigid‐Flexible Synergistic Nanofibrous Textiles for Mechanically Robust Radiative Cooling
title_en: Bio‐Inspired Rigid‐Flexible Synergistic Nanofibrous Textiles for Mechanically Robust Radiative Cooling
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) textiles offer an efficient pathway for personal thermal management. However, the inherent conflict between optical performance and mechanical robustness remains a formidable challenge. Although elastomer‐based electrospun nonwovens serve as a potential solution, they typically necessitate high nano‐filler loading for sufficient reflectance, which inevitably weakens interfacial bonding, leading to performance degradation and even structural failure during cyclic deformation. Herein, inspired by spider silk, we propose a filler‐free biomimetic rigid‐flexible synergy strategy regulated by dynamic hydrogen bonding. Via coaxial electrospinning, a robust TPU@PVDF‐HFP film (RTPF) comprising a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) core and a polyvinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene (PVDF‐HFP) sheath is engineered. The RTPF demonstrates outstanding mechanical strength (10.17 MPa) and elongation (301.34%), exhibiting superior mechanical and spectral stability with a mere 10.53% residual strain and 1.58% degradation after 1000 cycles at 30% strain. Attributed to high solar reflectance (96.2%) and long‐wave infrared emittance (92.5%), the RTPF achieves an average/maximum temperature reduction of 21.3/25.4°C on uncovered heated‐pad under 950 W·m − 2 irradiation. Remarkably, it exhibits exceptional stability against rigorous washing and extreme environments (high/low temperatures and acid/alkali conditions). title_zh: Bioinspired Homologous Gradient Interphase Sustains Phase‐Change Buffering and Radiative Cooling Under Thermal Shocks
title_en: Bioinspired Homologous Gradient Interphase Sustains Phase‐Change Buffering and Radiative Cooling Under Thermal Shocks
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Coupling phase‐change buffering with passive radiative cooling offers complementary continuous and transient regulation for personal thermal management (PTM). In fibrous systems, however, repeated phase transitions drive molecular rearrangement and thermomechanical stress accumulation, causing fiber deformation, pore collapse, and irreversible deterioration of radiative cooling performance. Herein, inspired by graded stress transfer in mussel byssus, we develop a homologous gradient interphase strategy to construct a core–gradient interphase–shell fibrous membrane (Ho‐GIFM) for durable PTM. During coaxial electrospinning, homologous polyethylene glycol‐based polyurethanes interdiffuse and entangle across the interface, while in situ UV crosslinking stabilizes the interphase. This structure redistributes phase‐change‐induced strain and constrains long‐range chain rearrangement, preserving phase‐change functionality and porous fiber networks. Ho‐GIFM exhibits a broad solid‐solid phase‐transition window (30.2–51.5°C) with a competitive melting enthalpy (60.2 J g −1 ). Notably, after 100 alternating thermal shocks between −40 and 80°C, Ho‐GIFM retains 99.0% of its initial solar reflectance versus only 74.5% for the heterogeneous counterpart, together with 99.9% mid‐infrared emissivity retention. Furthermore, it delivers a calculated daytime net radiative cooling power of 101.9 W m −2 and achieves an average synthetic‐skin temperature reduction of 14.9°C. This work provides an interfacial design strategy for durable PTM and multicomponent functional fibers.

title_zh: Co-Assembled MOF@SiO2 Nanostructures for Superhydrophobic and Electrically Insulating Radiative Cooling Coatings
title_en: Co-Assembled MOF@SiO2 Nanostructures for Superhydrophobic and Electrically Insulating Radiative Cooling Coatings
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology, characterized by zero-energy cooling capability, has shown great promise for thermal management of high-voltage electrical equipment. However, such application scenarios impose stringent multifunctional requirements on PRC coatings, including superhydrophobicity to resist surface contamination, as well as high electrical insulation strength to prevent surface flashover. Here, we report a co-assembly strategy for constructing multifunctional PRC coatings through the in situ integration of a metal-organic framework (MOF) with a silica precursor. The appropriately tailored bandgap (Eg = 4.25 eV) of the MOF, slightly exceeding the upper photon-energy bound of the measured solar band (4.13 eV), enables suppressed solar absorption while affording a strong mid-infrared emissivity. Meanwhile, the high-Eg SiO2 shell effectively passivates intrinsic insulation defects and the high surface energy associated with MOFs, thereby enhancing both dielectric reliability and superhydrophobicity. Consequently, the optimized PRC coating delivered a temperature drop of 10.6 ± 0.5 °C during outdoor testing, together with robust superhydrophobicity (153.7°) and high wet flashover strength (15.6 kV/cm). This work advances PRC coatings beyond conventional thermal regulation by integrating radiative cooling, surface self-cleaning, and electrical insulation into a unified material platform, opening new opportunities for passive thermal management of high-voltage electrical equipment.

title_zh: Design of Bioinspired Ordered Materials for Spectral Modulation
title_en: Design of Bioinspired Ordered Materials for Spectral Modulation

abstract_en: Conspectus Spectral modulation, the precise control over light reflection, transmission, absorption, and scattering, has become a transformative approach in areas such as smart windows, adaptive camouflage, radiative cooling, anticounterfeiting, and photovoltaics. Typical strategies primarily rely on tuning the intrinsic properties of electrochromic, thermochromic, or photochromic materials. Yet, these material-driven approaches still suffer from limited color purity, narrow tunability, slow response, and poor multifunction integration. An emerging alternative is to treat structural order as an independent physical design dimension. By organizing nanoscale building blocks into periodic, hierarchical, or reconfigurable architectures, one can manipulate light through Bragg diffraction, Mie scattering, plasmonic resonance, and graded-index effects. These mechanisms are difficult to access by chemical composition alone. Nature provides a rich library of such ordered designs. Photonic crystals, multilayers, porous networks, and graded-index arrays in organisms achieve efficient reflection, absorption, and transmission under ambient conditions. These biological systems show that precise control over orientation, periodicity, layer spacing, and refractive-index contrast can produce optical functions far beyond those of homogeneous materials. Translating these biological blueprints into synthetic stimuli-responsive systems offers a route from static structural control to dynamic and intelligent spectral regulation. title_zh: Green Radiative Cooling and Antimicrobial Materials Based on Polylactic Acid Oligomer Hexagonal Microspheres
title_en: Green Radiative Cooling and Antimicrobial Materials Based on Polylactic Acid Oligomer Hexagonal Microspheres
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Thermal management by passive radiative cooling materials can save energy and reduce emission of green-house gas remarkably compared with traditional air-conditioner cooling. However, few of these materials are degradable, thus their disposal may lead to another environmental problem. Meanwhile, the COVID-19 pandemic and other infectious diseases have raised the requirement of hygienic and antimicrobial performance. This work reports a discovery that polylactic acid oligomer (PLAO) material possesses radiative cooling effect, wide-spectrum antimicrobial property and degradability, simultaneously. The radiative cooling effect is attribute to the hexagonal microsphere geometry and nanotexture of polylactic acid oligomer (PLAO) crystals, which enhance the reflectivity in the solar spectrum through multiple scattering effect and exhibit high emissivity in the mid-infrared atmospheric window. Hierarchically porous PLAO coating material realizes an apparent temperature reduction of 6.8 ℃ under irradiation of solar spectrum (AM 1.5). The material also shows wide-spectrum antimicrobial and anti-viral properties against coronaviruses (including COVID-19 virus), gram-positive bacteria, gram-negative bacteria, fungi and multidrug resistant bacteria.

title_zh: Multiscale Freestanding Vertically Aligned CNT Heat Sink Enabling Multimodal Heat Dissipation by Conduction, Convection, and Radiation
title_en: Multiscale Freestanding Vertically Aligned CNT Heat Sink Enabling Multimodal Heat Dissipation by Conduction, Convection, and Radiation
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: A vertically aligned carbon nanotube (VACNT)-based heat sink is demonstrated for passive multimodal thermal management applicable for electronic and semiconductor devices. The VACNT enables multimodal heat dissipation through axial conduction, convection facilitated by its nanoporous morphology, and radiation enabled by its superior emissivity. While conventional metallic heat sinks suffer from low surface emissivity and require complex post-processing to enhance radiative cooling, the proposed VACNT overcomes these limitations by providing an inherent multiscale structural hierarchy without secondary surface treatments. The thermal conductivity of the freestanding VACNT (500 to 1500 µm heights) is characterized using laser flash analysis and differential scanning calorimetry as 32 to 40 W/mK. Evaluated on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W platform, the 1500 µm-high VACNT heat sink decreases the peak CPU temperature by 10.7°C compared with a bare CPU. The VACNT can be patterned into the topographic architecture to further improve heat dissipation by increasing the surface area, achieving a 6.7°C lower peak CPU temperature than a conventional aluminum heat sink. Cyclic stability test confirms consistent thermal performance over repeated use. The VACNT practically allows various configurational engineering by molding, rolling, scissoring, and tiling, showcasing its versatility for diverse thermal management applications.

title_zh: Optically clear mesoporous silica aerogels for passive daytime radiative cooling
title_en: Optically clear mesoporous silica aerogels for passive daytime radiative cooling
authors_short: Abhinav Bhanawat；Refet Ali Yalçın；Patricia E. McNeil 等
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: This study demonstrates the use of silica aerogel monoliths as optically transparent radiative cooling materials exhibiting near-unity emissivity in the 8–13 μm atmospheric transparency window. Silica is widely used for radiative cooling applications due to favorable optical properties. However, dense silica exhibits a reflectance peak around 9–9.5 μm due to the Reststrahlen effect, lowering emissivity near the blackbody peak (λ = 9.7 μm) at 300 K which substantially reduces cooling power. Previous approaches used complex photonic structures to enhance emissivity of silica-based radiative cooling materials. Here, a mesoporous microstructure of aerogels is demonstrated to eliminate this characteristic reflectance peak. The nanoparticles (∼4–5 nm radius) and pores (size distribution peak ∼9–20 nm) constituting the aerogel were much smaller than visible wavelengths, minimizing scattering and enabling >90% transmittance. Spectral emissivity and solar absorptance of these aerogels on metallic substrates were determined experimentally and numerically, showing high radiative cooling potential without needing complex nanostructures.

title_zh: Angle-confined bipolar emission for radiative cooling
title_en: Angle-confined bipolar emission for radiative cooling
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Radiative cooling offers a promising strategy to mitigate global warming by passively dissipating heat into outer space. While conventional strategies-based spectral emission control is approaching its physical limits, angular emission control has emerged as a new avenue for improving radiative cooling performance. However, the theoretical limits and cooling potential of idealized angle-confined emitters, particularly under varying surface inclinations and dynamic thermodynamic trade-offs, remain largely unexplored. Here, we introduce and validate a comprehensive theoretical framework to evaluate the cooling potential of angle-confined bipolar thermal emission. Inspired by the directional radiation characteristics of the Berreman mode, we establish an idealized, polarization-insensitive bipolar emission model to systematically investigate its performance across all possible surface inclinations from horizontal to vertical. Our findings reveal that such bipolar emitters consistently surpass isotropic counterparts by optimally balancing beneficial skyward radiation against detrimental ground-induced thermal loads, achieving a theoretical temperature reduction of up to 14.6 K at a 55 ° tilt angle. This work not only provides a generalized design methodology for angle-confined radiative coolers but also reveals the profound thermodynamic limits of bipolar emission, offering fundamental physical insights for next-generation directional thermal management.

abstract_zh: 辐射冷却纺织品（RCT）作为一种可行的户外环境热管理解决方案，已被证实能显著提升热舒适度。考虑到不同气候区不同季节的制冷需求存在时间差异，本研究提出了一种针对个人可穿戴辐射冷却服装的光学设计优化方法。研究分析了人体皮肤、服装和环境之间的热传递过程，并建立了用于预测热舒适度的人体模型。随后，通过比较棉质纺织品和RCT的性能，评估了穿着RCT所带来的热舒适度提升，并详细讨论了气象条件对穿着RCT者热舒适度的影响。为了提高RCT从制冷季节到过渡季节的长期穿着热舒适度，本研究提出了一种根据区域气候特征确定RCT光学特性的优化方法。最后，系统分析了优化后的RCT在中国不同气候区的热舒适度性能。结果表明，在中国不同气候带，穿着优化 RCT 的个体在最热的月份中，超过 88% 的时间可以保持在热舒适区内。

title_zh: Hydration‐Induced Environmentally‐Adaptive Thermal Management with Microphase Separated Hydrogel
title_en: Hydration‐Induced Environmentally‐Adaptive Thermal Management with Microphase Separated Hydrogel
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT The heat stress associated with extreme weather has paved the way for the rapid development of passive cooling techniques, but they are unable to tolerate fluctuating thermal and hydric environments, and their cooling power is more than halved under harsh conditions. Reliable multimodal thermal management techniques to couple with dynamic weather conditions are highly sought‐after. Herein, we develop a phase‐separated hydrogel via water‐induced microphase separation of waterborne polyurethane with the assistance of a hygroscopic layered network for hierarchical structure engineering. The obtained hydrogel undergoes hydration‐induced structural evolution from a compact solid monolith to a layered porous architecture, delivering a solar modulation capacity of ∼0.8 together with a high mid‐infrared emissivity of ∼0.95. Such optical features enable the hydrogel to achieve dynamic thermal regulation with a 9°C temperature span and sub‐ambient radiative cooling (∼6°C) under direct solar radiation. Additionally, via in situ incorporation of a light absorber or hygroscopic agent, the hydrogel is endowed with dual‐mode solar heating/cooling functionality and synergistic dehumidification‐cooling performance, respectively. Furthermore, the manufacturing process for the as‐proposed hydrogel is green, sustainable, and scalable, which permits industrial‐size hydrogels with combinations of stability, durability, sustainability, and processability. This work provides a promising candidate to meet the need for integrated thermoregulatory systems for environment‐specific adaptation.

abstract_en: ABSTRACT Passive daytime radiative cooling offers a sustainable cooling strategy by simultaneously reflecting solar radiation and emitting thermal radiation through the mid‐infrared transparent window. However, the coolers that achieve sub‐ambient daytime cooling typically appear white or silver, limiting their use in applications where colored appearances are required. Herein, we report a colored cooler (CoCooler) with a sandwich structure that decouples visible coloration from near‐infrared solar heating. The CoCooler integrates a transparent polydimethylsiloxane emission layer, an inorganic‐colorant‐containing layer, an isolation layer, and a porous radiative cooling layer. The sandwich structure enables selective visible absorption for color generation, strong near‐infrared reflection to minimize solar heating, and broadband mid‐infrared emission for radiative heat dissipation. The red, yellow, and blue CoCoolers exhibit vivid color while maintaining high solar reflectance of 90.70%, 91.58%, and 89.89%, respectively, and high mid‐infrared emissivity of 0.982, 0.983, and 0.982. Under outdoor sunlight, the CoCoolers achieve sub‐ambient temperature drops of 3.7°C–5.4°C, and are 33.3°C–42.2°C cooler than the commercial‐colored paints with similar chromaticity. abstract_en: Thermal management by controlling radiative energy exchange has emerged as a sustainable route for regulating temperature and reducing energy consumption. Conventional thermal–management surfaces with static optical properties continue to find it challenging to respond to dynamic changes in ambient temperature, solar irradiation, or operating conditions. Strongly correlated oxides, which undergo insulator–metal transitions under external stimuli such as heat, electric field, light, or ion intercalation, enable reversible modulation of their optical constants for dynamic control of radiative energy exchange. This review summarizes recent advances in utilizing insulator–metal transitions in correlated oxides for dynamic thermal management. We first describe the energy balance of adaptive thermal surfaces within the solar and atmospheric spectra and map the optical parameters of materials to device–level thermal regulation performance. Then, three representative correlated oxides, including tungsten trioxide, vanadium dioxide (VO2), and perovskite rare–earth nickelates (RNiO3), are discussed in their transition behaviors and optical responses across multiple wavelength regions. abstract_en: With the escalating global energy crisis and environmental challenges, radiative cooling textiles have emerged as a promising energy-free thermal management solution. However, existing cooling fabrics primarily focus on enhancing optical properties like solar reflectance and infrared emissivity, often neglecting the critical role of nonradiative heat dissipation (conduction and convection) while also facing challenges in scalability, durability, and comfort. To address these limitations, this study presents a scalably manufactured polyethylene/boron nitride (HDPE/BN) composite fabric fabricated via industrial melt spinning and weaving. By uniformly incorporating BN sheets into HDPE fibers, the composite fabric achieves enhanced solar reflectivity (86%) and mid-infrared emissivity (89.3%) due to the high refractive index, efficient Mie scattering, and intrinsic infrared absorption features of BN. title_zh: Sustainable Polypropylene Composites with Rod-Like Calcium Carbonate Particles Derived from Ocean-Mineralization-Based Carbon Capture
title_en: Sustainable Polypropylene Composites with Rod-Like Calcium Carbonate Particles Derived from Ocean-Mineralization-Based Carbon Capture
authors_short: Taehyeon Kim；Jeongsik E. Park；MinJeong Kim 等
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Abstract Efficiently utilizing captured carbon as high-value materials is a cornerstone of achieving global carbon neutrality. In this study, we present a sustainable approach to upcycle calcium carbonate (CaCO3) microparticles, synthesized via ocean-mineralization-based carbon capture, into functional fillers to enhance the performance of polypropylene (PP) composites. The unique morphology of mineralized rod-like CaCO3 (MRC) influenced the mechanical and rheological properties of PP composites compared with commercial rhombohedral CaCO3 (CRC). The MRC particles, characterized by a high aspect ratio and narrow size distribution, significantly enhanced both Young’s modulus and storage modulus of the PP composites. To improve interfacial adhesion, surface modification with stearic acid (SA) was employed, which effectively promoted ductile fracture and energy dissipation. Consequently, the PP composite reinforced with 30 wt % of surface-treated MRC exhibited a simultaneous 2.3-fold increase in tensile toughness and a 1.2-fold increase in Young’s modulus compared with neat PP. In addition to mechanical reinforcement, the PP composite films showed high solar reflectance and mid-infrared emissivity, demonstrating their potential for radiative cooling applications. Life-cycle and techno-economic assessments further showed that the incorporation of MRC-SA reduced the carbon footprint and estimated production cost of the composites by up to 35% and 26% compared with neat PP, respectively.

title_zh: Dynamic Infrared Regulation and Passive Radiative Cooling of Electrospun Fabrics
title_en: Dynamic Infrared Regulation and Passive Radiative Cooling of Electrospun Fabrics
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Abstract Global warming and rapid urbanization have exacerbated extreme heat waves and urban heat island effects, posing severe threats to ecological stability and human well-being. Traditional thermal regulation materials generally suffer from inferior environmental adaptability and insufficient dynamic thermal modulation capability, restricting their practical deployment. Herein, inspired by Rayleigh scattering theory, we report the fabrication of polyamide 6/cetyltrimethylammonium bromide composite fibrous membranes via a modified electrospinning technique. The diameter of electrospun nanoyarns is precisely controlled at approximately 200 nm, which effectively suppresses infrared scattering loss and optimizes the infrared radiative performance of the materials. Within the atmospheric transparent window of 8–14 μm, the resultant composite fabrics exhibit an infrared transmittance enhancement of ∼40%. At thermal equilibrium conditions, the as-prepared materials deliver outstanding passive radiative cooling performance, achieving a temperature reduction of nearly 15 °C. This work presents a feasible strategy for the rational design of high-performance adaptive thermal management textiles. It also offers promising perspectives for mitigating extreme heat hazards and developing urban thermal regulation systems.

abstract_en: This chapter provides a comprehensive framework for passive thermal management technologies in the modern automotive systems that emphasizes on the growing importance in the domain of electric, hybrid, and autonomous vehicles. The key passive mechanisms discussed are the heat pipes, vapor chambers, phase-change materials, thermoelectric generators, and passive radiative cooling for enhancing heat transfer rate, stabilizing component temperatures, and reducing the load on active cooling systems. The chapter highlights how these technologies enable high heat flux dissipation and provide cooling without external energy input. Emerging trends such as multi-material thermal composites, AI-driven topology optimization, hybrid passive-active architectures, advanced radiative coatings, and integrated thermal-structural designs are explored as pathways for improving system efficiency, reliability, and vehicle range. Together, these innovations establish a robust foundation for next-generation automotive thermal management, enabling safer, more efficient, and environmentally sustainable mobility platforms.

abstract_en: Abstract Radiative cooling technology passively dissipates surface heat to outer space through the atmospheric window (8–13 μm), providing an innovative pathway for continuous cooling with zero energy consumption and zero carbon emissions. The core challenge for high-performance daytime radiative cooling lies in strict spectral selectivity: A solar reflectance exceeding 90% in the solar spectrum band (0.3–2.5 μm) is required to minimize solar heating, while an infrared emissivity higher than 90% must be maintained within the atmospheric window to maximize radiative heat dissipation. This review systematically provides the latest advances in radiative cooling materials and structures in recent years, centered on the core driving force of “spectral selective structural design”. According to the optical modulation hierarchy of structural design ranging from random to precise, existing research is categorized into two major technical pathways: (1) Random scattering structures based on intrinsic material properties, including polymer films and functional coatings. Achieving this combination in sustainable biomass-derived materials remains challenging. Here, a multifunctional sodium alginate-based aerogel (SPCA) was fabricated via directional freezing and reinforced by a dual-cross-linked framework formed through PA-mediated hydrogen bonding and Ca2+ coordination. The resulting network produced a denser, more uniform honeycomb-like porous structure, thereby strengthening the aerogel skeleton. SPCA achieved a compressive strength of 4.57 MPa and a compressive modulus of 37.97 MPa, along with improved water stability. Despite moderate structural densification, SPCA retained a low thermal conductivity of 0.044 W m–1 K–1 and outperformed several commercial insulation materials under both hot and cold conditions. title_en: Regulation Mechanisms, Material Systems and Application Progress of Dynamic Radiative Cooling
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Radiative cooling achieves low-energy heat rejection via radiative heat exchange between the ground surface and outer space. Nevertheless, static materials possess fixed spectral properties and tend to trigger overcooling in winter, at night or under low thermal loads. This paper reviews active regulation, passive self-adaptation, near-zero energy consumption and active-passive synergy mechanisms. It compares the regulation characteristics of electrochromism, mechanical/fluid switching, thermally induced phase change, thermosensitive hydrogel, humidity response and bistable structures. Applications in buildings, electronic devices, smart textiles, vehicle energy storage and aerospace thermal management are summarized. Finally, engineering challenges including cycle life, outdoor weather resistance, encapsulation, large-area fabrication, energy consumption accounting and testing standards are discussed.

title_en: Angular solar absorption and thermal energy storage seasonally modulate radiative cooling

abstract_en: Passive daytime radiative cooling materials (RCs) maintain low surface temperatures under sunlight and can reduce building cooling loads and urban overheating. However, RCs with static optical properties overcool in cold seasons, and adaptive RCs proposed to date rely on temperature/humidity to switch their optical/radiative properties. Further, they address either daytime or nighttime response and are subject to ageing and to false switching on mild sunlit winter days. Here, we propose a system to seasonally modulate RCs with angular solar absorption, achieved with L-shaped fins, and with thermal energy storage (TES), implemented with phase change materials (PCMs) and concrete mass. abstract_en: Developing high-performance passive radiative cooling coatings (PRCC) with high thermal conductivity for fast heat dissipation from self-heating objects remains a significant challenge. In this study, a nanocellulose-mediated Pickering emulsion strategy was employed to construct a uniform hexagonal boron nitride (BN) thermal network within PRCC. Benefiting from the Pickering emulsion template stabilized by TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibrils (TOCNF), BN nanosheets and other functional inorganic nanoparticles were uniformly dispersed in the PRCC matrix, forming a continuous and homogeneous thermally conductive network. This structural design endowed the PRCC with excellent thermal conductivity, high solar reflectance in the solar spectrum (0.3–2.5 μm), and strong emissivity in the “atmospheric window” (ATSW, 8–13 μm). Specifically, the thermal conductivity of the TOCNF-BN-modified PRCC reached 2.28 ± 0.15 W·m−1·K−1, which was significantly higher than that of the pristine PRCC. The coating exhibited a solar reflectivity of ~87% and an emissivity of ~93% in the ATSW. Outdoor model temperature tests indicated that the internal temperature of the PRCC-TOCNF-BN-coated metal cabinet was 9.6 °C lower than that of the bare cabinet and 6.7 °C lower than the cabinet coated with pristine PRCC. This novel approach of using Pickering emulsion templates to fabricate highly thermally conductive radiative cooling coatings provides a new strategy for the development of high-performance and multifunctional radiative cooling materials for thermal management applications.

title_en: THE PHOTONIC THERMAL SHIELD ADVANCED PASSIVE RADIATIVE COOLING MATERIALS FOR ZERO-ENERGY THERMAL MANAGEMENT A Unified Framework for Nanophotonic Engineering, Thermodynamic Optimization, and Sustainable Urban Infrastructure

abstract_en: THE PHOTONIC THERMAL SHIELD by Dr. M.K.A. El-Rakhawi (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23511418) details an engineering framework for Passive Radiative Cooling (PRC) materials, enabling zero-energy, sub-ambient thermal management. It exploits the atmospheric transparency window (8–13 μm) to radiate heat directly into space. This requires dual optical properties: >95% solar reflectance via hierarchical bimodal particle distributions (100–1000 nm) for efficient Mie scattering, and >90% mid-infrared emittance via phonon-polariton resonance in polymers like PVDF. Net cooling power is modeled as P_cool = P_rad - P_atm - (1 - ρ_solar)I_solar - P_cond+conv. The framework transitions PRC from lab-scale lithography to scalable, solution-processed polymer nanocomposites using roll-to-roll manufacturing. Applications include urban heat island mitigation, photovoltaic rear-side cooling (requiring high thermal conductivity to the cell and high MIR emissivity to the sky), and radiative textiles. The IP framework excludes abstract natural laws (per Alice/Myriad), strictly protecting specific engineered nanophotonic architectures and scalable manufacturing protocols.

title_zh: Robust Radiative Cooling in Functionalizable Silica Microsphere Paints

authors_short: Jorge Burgos；José Rodrigo Magaña；Ares Lladós 等
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Abstract Disordered coatings based on silica microspheres provide a scalable and robust platform for passive daytime radiative cooling. While particle-size optimization is often considered critical for enhancing solar scattering, the role of microsphere diameter once a coating operates in the multiple-scattering regime remains unclear. Here, we characterize the radiative cooling performance of disordered, multiply scattering photonic glass coatings with diameters ranging from 2 to 8 μm, deposited on a highly reflective substrate. Despite measurable differences in microscopic scattering properties, both the spectral radiative response and the net cooling performance are robust to variations in particle diameter within the investigated range. Outdoor thermal measurements reveal nearly identical steady-state temperature reductions across the full size range. These results identify this robustness as a property of the complete coating–substrate architecture: in the solar range, multiple scattering and the reflective substrate act together to maintain high reflectance, while in the mid-infrared range, the response is dominated by the intrinsic Si–O absorption of the silica layer. This robustness enables microsphere size to be selected based on surface chemistry or processing constraints without compromising cooling performance.

title_zh: 用于被动辐射冷却的可修复热固性弹性体材料
title_en: Healable Thermoset Elastomeric Materials for Passive Radiative Cooling
abstract_zh: 零能耗的被动辐射冷却（PRC）技术是一种高效的热管理策略，有助于构建可持续发展的社会。然而，制备具有固有延展性/尺寸稳定性、高效自愈能力，且能适应不规则形状并延长使用寿命的PRC材料仍然是一项重大挑战。本研究提出了一种基于交联弹性网络的机械强度高且可自愈的PRC薄膜设计原理。该网络结合了物理相互作用和动态共价键，可通过无机涂层和微/纳米多孔分级结构进行调控，同时保持延展性和自愈能力。这种热固性弹性体PRC薄膜具有可扩展性，且具有高太阳反射率和长波红外发射率，即使经过物理损伤和自愈过程，仍能保持优异的冷却性能。它在夏季展现出卓越的屋顶冷却能力，在冬季则能有效保护冰雕。热固性弹性体PRC薄膜的可扩展合成为实现柔性、稳定且可自愈的PRC材料开辟了新的途径，具有广阔的实际应用前景。
abstract_en: Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology with zero-energy uptake is an efficient thermal management strategy for the development of sustainable society. Fabrication of PRC materials with intrinsic extensibility/dimensional stability and efficient healability that can adapt to irregular shapes with prolonged lifetime remains a significant challenge. The present study introduces a design principle for mechanically robust and healable PRC films based on a cross-linked elastomeric network with combined physical interactions and dynamic covalent bonds, which can be readily modulated by inorganic coating and micro-/nano-porous hierarchical architectures while retaining extensibility and healability. Such thermosetting elastomeric PRC films are scalable with strong solar reflectance and long-wave infrared emittance, realizing excellent cooling performance even after physical damage and healing process. It demonstrates excellent roof cooling ability in summer yet efficient ice-sculpture preservation function in winter. The scalable synthesis of thermoset elastomeric PRC films opens up new pathways to realize flexible, stable and healable PRC materials, highly promising for practical applications.

title_zh: Adaptive and Multicolored Electrochromic Smart Window with Transparent–Opaque Switchable Radiative Cooling
title_en: Adaptive and Multicolored Electrochromic Smart Window with Transparent–Opaque Switchable Radiative Cooling
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Transparent radiative-cooling windows can reduce cooling demand while preserving daylighting, yet high solar transmission becomes undesirable under strong solar irradiation. Although existing electrochromic windows can regulate solar transmittance, simultaneously achieving strong solar rejection, radiative heat dissipation, and wide-gamut coloration remains challenging. Here, we develop dynamic colorful radiative cooling windows by integrating planar coupled nanocavities with reversible silver electrodeposition. Electrochemically controlled Ag deposition/stripping reconfigures Fabry-Pérot resonances, enabling reversible switching between colored transparent and highly reflective colored opaque states while retaining high mid-infrared emissivity. The devices can achieve >40% modulation in average visible transmittance and cover 99.5% of the sRGB color gamut. Under outdoor conditions, they exhibit temperature drops of ∼7.0 °C compared to conventional glass and ∼8.7 °C relative to commercial electrochromic glass. This work provides a versatile platform for dynamic optical regulation with diverse requirements, paving the way for next-generation multifunctional smart windows, building envelopes, and smart photonic devices.

title_zh: Biobased Boston Ivy‐Inspired Cryogel Integrating Radiative Cooling and Phase Change Energy Storage for Adaptive Thermal Regulation
title_en: Biobased Boston Ivy‐Inspired Cryogel Integrating Radiative Cooling and Phase Change Energy Storage for Adaptive Thermal Regulation
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Boston ivy is a traditional plant for building heat management through shading and transpiration. Inspired by its “vine‐leaf” system, we design a bionic cryogel that functionalizes daytime cooling and nighttime thermal buffering, promoting sustainable and comfortable housing and living environments. The aligned channels mimic vine tendrils, delivering an ultralow radial thermal conductivity (0.035 W m −1 ·K −1 ), high solar reflectance (95.28%), and high infrared emissivity (97.04%). Embedded phase‐change materials (PCMs) present leaf‐like, functionalized structures that store excess solar energy during the daytime and release latent heat at night, achieving 6.2°C sub‐ambient cooling under sunlight. In darkness, the stored latent heat is released, keeping the cryogel 2.4°C above ambient and preventing nocturnal overcooling. This spatiotemporal synergy between daytime radiative cooling and nighttime heat release enables climate‐adaptive thermal management, reducing the urban heat buildup with no need for electricity consumption. Our bionic design shifts thermal regulation from passive adaptation to active thermal planning using low carbon footprint materials as proven by life cycle assessment (LCA), offering a more sustainable pathway for energy‐efficient buildings.

title_zh: Radiative Cooling Floating Covers Cool Lakes and Suppress Evaporation
title_en: Radiative Cooling Floating Covers Cool Lakes and Suppress Evaporation
authors_short: Hafiz Muhammad Asfahan；Siyuan Jia；Syeda Mishal Zahra 等
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Globally, warmer lakes disrupt thermal balance, causing hypoxia, salinization, biodiversity loss, and increased evaporation. Conventional floating covers used to reduce evaporation absorb sunlight and warm the underlying water, limiting suppression efficiency to less than the coverage ratio (η eff /Φ ≤ 1). Here, we break this limit by developing Superhydrophobic Radiative Cooling Covers (SRCC) via multi‐level structural design. SRCC actively cools the water surface by combining high solar reflectance, strong mid‐infrared emission, and superhydrophobicity. Experiments show SRCC lowers water temperature by 2.2°C versus uncovered water, achieving 93.1± 0.1% evaporation suppression at 91% coverage, yielding η eff /Φ > 1.0 for the first time. Large‑scale simulations for nine Chinese lakes indicate that SRCC reduces water temperature by 4.87°C (vs. no cover) and by 12.44 °C (vs. black covers). This cooling could increase annual freshwater reserves by 10.78 km 3 across China under full deployment, equivalent to 20.9 L per person per day. Unattainable with conventional covers, SRCC uniquely mitigates thermal accumulation while enhancing freshwater storage, providing a quantifiable engineering solution to climate‑driven water stress and enabling adaptive lake ecosystem management across regional and global scales.

abstract_en: ABSTRACT Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) provides a zero‐energy thermal management strategy. Thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) is suitable for electrospun cooling textiles due to its spinnability, flexibility, and high infrared emissivity, but it suffers from UV‐induced photothermal accumulation and aging. Here, we implement a nanoscale fluorescence‐competitive absorption strategy by incorporating fluorescent microspheres (FMs) whose excitation spectrum fully covers the UV absorption band of TPU. These FMs convert UV photons into visible emission, simultaneously reducing photothermal conversion, enhancing UV stability, and enabling coloration. A highly reflective, hierarchical nanofibrous underlayer with a hierarchical fiber‐diameter distribution, fabricated via high‐concentration electrospinning, further achieves broadband scattering, thereby yielding an overall effective solar reflectance (ESR sol ) of 96.7%. abstract_en: ABSTRACT Adaptive thermal regulation across diurnal and seasonal cycles remains a critical challenge for energy‐efficient buildings. A switchable dual‐mode Janus‐structured composite is developed by integrating a polyoxymethylene fiber/acrylate resin/BaSO 4 aerogel cooling layer with a graphene aerogel/paraffin wax (PW) phase‐change composite heating layer to achieve synergistic passive radiative cooling, solar‐Joule heating, and latent‐heat storage. The heating layer exhibits high thermal conductivity, high solar‐to‐latent heat conversion efficiency, high latent heat capacity, and high electrical conductivity. This permits a maximum sub‐ambient temperature rise of 17.4°C across the day. The cooling layer delivers a solar reflectivity of 96.2%, a mid‐infrared emissivity of 94.0%, and a low thermal conductivity of 0.053 W m −1 K −1 , achieving a maximum sub‐ambient temperature drop of 21.3°C and a genuine radiative net cooling power of 110.4 W m −2 , with an additional transient thermal buffering provided by the latent heat of PW (239.7 J g −1 ). Outdoor tests verify diurnal regulation and paraffin‐induced temperature hysteresis. Building energy simulations across 15 Chinese cities demonstrate annual energy savings exceeding 10.8% in most regions, with reductions of 9.5 and 15.1 MJ m −2 in heating and cooling demands, respectively. This work provides an effective strategy for all‐weather thermal management and sustainable energy savings under diverse climatic conditions.

abstract_en: Abstract Passive radiative cooling is a promising thermal management technology that requires no external energy to achieve cooling. By emitting thermal radiation through the atmospheric transparency window to the cold outer space, it can maintain a temperature below the ambient environment. In this work, a broadband selective-emissivity emitter for daytime radiative cooling is proposed. The presented emitter achieves strong solar reflectivity and enhanced thermal emissivity within the atmospheric window. Simulation findings demonstrate that the proposed thin-film structure possesses excellent reflective performance from 0.3 μ m to 2.5 μ m, achieving an average reflectivity of 0.98. Meanwhile, an average emissivity of 0.93 is obtained from 8 μ m to 13 μ m, enabling efficient thermal radiation to outer space. Owing to its broadband selective-emission characteristics, the emitter effectively enhances the spectral matching between thermal radiation and the atmospheric window. Based on thermal equilibrium equations, the net cooling heat flux of the emitter is determined to be 117.64 W m −2 under typical daytime conditions. Compared with conventional broadband emitters, the proposed structure concentrates thermal emission predominantly during the atmospheric window, exhibiting excellent broadband selective-emission characteristics. The proposed design also shows promising potential for energy-efficient buildings, electronic heat dissipation, and temperature regulation of photovoltaic systems.

abstract_en: Abstract Passive daytime radiative cooling lowers surface temperature without external power by reflecting solar radiation and emitting heat through the 8 - 13 um atmospheric window. This paper develops an integrated thermo-optical modeling and optimization framework for PDMS-based passive radiative cooling coatings, combining thin-film spectral analysis, multi-objective structural optimization, and robustness evaluation under practical uncertainties. A single-layer spectral-emissivity model is first established with thin-film optics and the transfer matrix method, then coupled with an energy-balance model to evaluate net cooling power under daytime conditions. To improve the thickness sensitivity of the single-layer baseline, a multilayer structure composed of PDMS, SiO 2 , Al 2 O 3 , and TiO 2 is optimized under multiple objectives, including solar rejection, window emissivity, thickness, and cost. A practical thermo-optical model further tests the optimized design under environmental forcing and manufacturing uncertainty. The results show that PDMS keeps low emissivity in the solar band, its atmospheric-window emissivity rises with thickness and gradually saturates, and the optimized multilayer design improves cooling performance while retaining practical robustness.

abstract_zh: 由于太阳反射和可见光吸收之间存在光谱权衡，开发兼具高太阳反射率和理想色彩（尤其是紫色）的被动辐射冷却（PRC）织物仍然极具挑战性。本文设计了一种“彩色-白色-彩色”三明治结构的超材料织物，旨在平衡美观性和冷却性能。该织物由光谱选择性的紫色表层和高反射率的散射芯层组成。表层由聚氨酯（TPU）纤维和紫色金属有机框架ZIF-67构成，能够选择性地吸收可见光并增强中红外发射；而TPU/ZnO纳米纤维芯层则通过强散射增强宽带太阳反射。通过空间上解耦色彩和反射，该织物实现了90.6%的高太阳反射率和94.6%的中红外发射率。户外测试表明，白天最大降温幅度约为5.2 ℃。模拟和真实皮肤评估均证实，与市售染色棉织物相比，该织物具有更优异的个人冷却性能。该织物还具有良好的透湿性和疏水性，水蒸气透过率约为24.01 mg·cm⁻² · h⁻¹ ，水接触角约为120 °，有利于汗液蒸发和散热。这项工作为设计兼具
abstract_en: Developing passive radiative cooling (PRC) fabrics that combine high solar reflectance with desirable coloration, particularly purple, remains challenging due to the spectral trade-off between solar reflection and visible light absorption. Here, a "colored-white-colored" sandwich-structured metafabric is designed to balance aesthetic appearance and cooling performance. The fabric consists of spectrally selective purple skin layers and a highly reflective scattering core. The skin layers, composed of polyurethane (TPU) fibers and purple metal-organic framework ZIF-67, enable selective visible light absorption and enhanced mid-infrared emission, while the TPU/ZnO nanofiber core enhances broadband solar reflection through strong scattering. By spatially decoupling coloration and reflection, the fabric achieves a high solar reflectance of 90.6% and a mid-infrared emissivity of 94.6%. Outdoor tests show a maximum sub-ambient cooling of about 5.2 oC during daytime. Simulated and real-skin evaluations confirm superior personal cooling performance compared with commercial dyed cotton fabrics. The fabric also exhibits good moisture permeability and hydrophobicity, with a water vapor transmission rate of ~24.01 mg·cm-2·h-1 and a water contact angle of ~120o, which facilitates sweat evaporation and heat dissipation. title_en: Chemistry and Structure of Birch Bark Support Passive Radiative Cooling
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Abstract White-barked birches extend to the northern limit of tree growth, and their bark is known to reduce solar damage during winter and early-spring by limiting solar heating and the incidence of harmful freeze-thaw events. The physical basis for this protection, however, has remained unclear. Here, we show that extracted betulin, the dominant triterpenoid responsible for the bark’s whiteness, and Himalayan birch bark, both exhibit passive radiative cooling. Under low solar irradiance, bark and betulin-pellets reach temperatures below that of a shaded reference, and pellets cool more than bark. The cooling arises from high solar reflectance, which suppresses solar heating, and substantial mid-infrared emission, which drives radiative heat loss toward outer space. These findings help explain how bark-whiteness may contribute to protecting birch trees from solar-induced thermal stress.

abstract_en: Abstract With the increasing demand for energy-efficient cooling technologies, passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) has emerged as a promising strategy for achieving subambient cooling without energy input. However, conventional PDRC materials typically rely on highly reflective white surfaces, limiting their applicability in scenarios requiring aesthetic diversity. A photoluminescent dual-layer colored radiative cooling composite film (CRC) is developed via continuous electrospinning technology. The film consists of a bottom reflective layer composed of PVDF-HFP nanofibers doped with SiO2/Al2O3 particles to enhance solar scattering, and a top photoluminescent layer incorporating fluorescent dyes for color generation. This dual-layer configuration enables the introduction of color while largely preserving high solar reflectance and mid-infrared emissivity. To accurately evaluate the optical performance of photoluminescent systems, a combined colorimetric–spectral characterization method (CS) is employed to decouple fluorescence-induced pseudoreflectance in the visible region. The resulting films exhibit a solar reflectance of ∼88% and an emissivity exceeding 97% within the atmospheric window (8–13 μm). abstract_en: Passive radiative cooling requires materials that combine high mid-infrared (MIR) emissivity within the atmospheric transparency window (8-13 µm) with minimal solar absorption, while maintaining scalability and long-term stability. Porous anodic alumina (PAA) is an attractive dielectric platform due to its intrinsic phonon-polariton infrared emission and electrochemically tunable nanostructure. However, achieving independent control of visible photonic properties and MIR emissivity within a single architecture remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate dual-spectral control of PAA photonic structures integrated with aluminum (Al) substrates using charge density-controlled sinusoidal pulse anodization. Periodic voltage modulation generates well-defined photonic stop bands (PSBs) in the visible range, enabling tunable structural coloration while preserving high MIR emissivity. Systematic pore widening produces a progressive blue shift of the PSB accompanied by non-monotonic reflectance changes, revealing distinct mechanisms governing spectral position and optical coherence. In contrast, MIR emissivity remains robust against variations in the visible photonic response, as confirmed by a constant-voltage reference sample. abstract_zh: 全球节能和个人热管理需要先进的被动辐射冷却纺织品，这种纺织品无需外部能量输入即可调节人体与周围环境（包括太阳、外太空、建筑物和地面）之间的辐射热通道。传统的辐射冷却纺织品通常设计成超白或银色以最大限度地反射太阳光，但可穿戴服装的实际应用要求最大限度减少光污染并兼顾美观的色彩。然而，纺织品的着色通常需要强烈的可见光吸收，这会显著降低冷却性能。因此，如何平衡冷却效果和美观色彩之间的这一根本难题已成为开发下一代彩色辐射冷却纺织品的核心挑战。本文综述了彩色辐射冷却纺织品的最新进展，重点关注基于光-纺织品相互作用的不同着色策略：颜料着色、光致发光着色和结构着色。本文对这些彩色纺织品的冷却性能进行了深入分析和阐述。此外，我们还系统地讨论了尚存的挑战，包括色彩冷却优化、长期耐久性、可扩展性，并展望了多功能可穿戴纺织品的未来发展机遇。本综述旨在为设计下一代彩色辐射冷却纺织品提供全面的指导，将热管理与色彩功能统一起来。

abstract_en: ABSTRACT Passive radiative cooling (PRC) offers a sustainable pathway for heat dissipation to outer space without energy input. Polymers have emerged as attractive platforms owing to their lightweight, flexibility, low cost, and structural tunability. This review highlights structure‐oriented strategies for polymer‐based PRC, categorized into fibrous, porous, photonic/meta, and hybrid composite designs. Fibrous networks enhance solar scattering while maintaining breathability; porous systems utilize multi‐scale pores for strong reflectance and broadband infrared emission; photonic/meta‐structures enable spectral selectivity and color control; and hybrids integrate inorganic fillers to achieve robustness and multifunctionality. Representative studies report solar reflectance above 98%, emissivity above 97%, and net cooling powers exceeding 100 W·m −2 under daytime conditions. Beyond performance, advances in eco‐friendly polymers, humidity‐tolerant structures, and scalable fabrication are emphasized. General design principles are summarized within a structure–property–performance framework, stressing broadband solar scattering, efficient IR emission, scalable processing, and interfacial engineering. abstract_zh: 彩色辐射冷却涂料在美学热管理方面具有巨大的潜力。然而，以往的研究要么局限于基于直觉的正向设计（这种方法成本过高，难以获得非直觉的最优设计），要么仅限于理想化光谱层面的优化。我们提出了一种基于机器学习的逆向设计框架，用于生成具有最佳冷却性能和所需颜色的涂料配方。通过将光子蒙特卡罗模拟与代理模型相结合，该方法弥合了理论光谱与实际应用之间的差距。我们的方法揭示了一种非直觉的“双窄带吸收”策略，与传统的加性吸收和单带减性吸收策略相比，该策略分别可将太阳辐射热功率降低高达 193 和 37 W/m² 。对 HSL 色彩空间的系统探索表明，在考虑实际材料限制的情况下，24% 的颜色可以实现低于环境温度的日间冷却效果。这一自动化流程为设计高性能、美观的辐射冷却涂料提供了实用的指导。
abstract_en: Colored radiative cooling paints offer immense potential for aesthetic thermal management. However, previous studies have been limited to either intuition-driven forward designs that are too expensive to yield non-intuitive optimal designs or to optimizations only at the level of idealized optical spectra. We present a machine-learning-enabled inverse design framework for generating paint formulations with optimal cooling performance and desired color. By integration of photon Monte Carlo simulations with surrogate modeling, this approach bridges the gap between theoretical spectra and physical realization. Our approach uncovers a non-intuitive “double narrow-band absorption” strategy that reduces solar heating power by up to 193 and 37 W/m 2 compared to conventional additive and single-band subtractive strategies, respectively. A systematic exploration of the HSL color space reveals that 24% of colors can achieve daytime subambient cooling when realistic material limitations are considered. This automated pipeline provides practical guidelines for designing high-performance, aesthetically tailored radiative cooling coatings.

abstract_zh: 一种光谱选择性 PVF 辐射冷却发射体（PRCE）实现 97.5%的太阳反射率和 94.4%的发射率（8–13 微米）。它抑制来自高温地面和建筑物的寄生热量：在城市峡谷中比宽带发射器低 1.9°C，在开阔田野中低于环境温度 2.4°C。PRCE 具有可扩展性、耐用性和自清洁性等显著优势。
abstract_en: Passive daytime radiative cooling offers a carbon‑free route to mitigate urban heat islands and reduce building energy use. Conventional broadband emitters, however, suffer from parasitic absorption of ambient thermal radiation from hot ground and adjacent buildings, severely compromising net cooling in dense urban settings. We present a scalable, spectrally selective radiative cooling coating that overcomes this urban penalty. By combining a phase‑inversion‑derived micro‑nano porous poly (vinyl fluoride) (PVF) layer with a reflective silver substrate, our emitter achieves a record spectral selectivity of 1.37, with 97.5% solar reflectance and 94.4% mid‑infrared emittance strictly confined to the atmospheric window (8_13 µm). In simulated urban canyon tests, the selective emitter stayed 1.9°C cooler than a broadband counterpart, effectively neutralizing heat gain from surrounding infrastructure. The coating also exhibits excellent scalability, adhesion, self‑cleaning ability, and chemical durability. By bridging performance, manufacturability, and resilience, this work offers a viable pathway for adopting radiative cooling in sustainable urban development.

abstract_en: Passive radiative cooling (PRC) has emerged as a promising zero-energy thermal management strategy for building energy conservation and device temperature regulation. However, conventional fabrication routes for cooling films typically involve complex procedures, and the pore structures are challenging to regulate, which limits spectral tunability and scalable manufacturing. Here, a simple and scalable water-induced phase separation strategy is developed to fabricate multiscale porous polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) radiative cooling films. Simulations reveal that pores with tunable porosity and diameter perturb the local electric field distribution, thereby enhancing backward scattering of incident light. By adjusting the water content, both the average pore size and porosity can be systematically controlled to optimize scattering behavior. The resulting porous PDMS film achieves an average solar reflectance of 67.5% and an infrared emissivity of 92.6%, exhibiting enhanced radiative cooling property. Xenon-lamp tests further confirm its promising cooling potential, achieving a reduced temperature of 16.3℃ compared to a wooden substrate. This work provides a cost-effective and structurally tunable strategy for fabricating porous PDMS-based radiative cooling materials, advancing the applicability in scalable thermal management system.

abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Personal thermal management (PTM) requires materials that can adapt to dynamically changing environments, yet most existing systems are limited to single-mode cooling or heating and lack tunable optical appearance. Here, we report a structurally colored photonic Janus film that enables switchable radiative cooling and solar heating within a single material platform. The cooling side is based on cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) photonic structures, providing high mid-infrared emissivity (up to 0.91) while enabling tunable structural color through pitch modulation, thereby achieving radiative cooling without sacrificing visual appearance. The heating side consists of a carbon nanotube (CNT) layer with high solar absorptivity (~92%), enabling efficient photothermal conversion, further enhanced by low-voltage Joule heating. By simply flipping the film, reversible switching between cooling and heating modes is achieved, allowing adaptation to varying thermal conditions. In addition, the system is compatible with continuous fabrication, enabling scalable production. This work demonstrates a dual-mode photonic thermal management system that integrates optical tunability with switchable thermal regulation, providing a viable pathway toward wearable microclimate control.

title_zh: Biomimetic Janus Fabric with Ice Plant Bubble‐Like Cell Structure for Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling and Energy Conversion for Wearable Applications
title_en: Biomimetic Janus Fabric with Ice Plant Bubble‐Like Cell Structure for Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling and Energy Conversion for Wearable Applications
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Smart textiles require advanced sensing capabilities, yet existing sensor‐integrated fabrics suffer from poor breathability, brittleness, and thermal vulnerability, restricting large‐scale deployment. Herein, inspired by the epidermal bubble‐like cell structure of ice plants, we developed an ultra‐lightweight Janus fabric, with a polyelectrolyte membrane as the key component—its inherent high stability, excellent ion conductivity, and good compatibility endow the fabric with superior structural flexibility and functional synergy. This design integrates passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) and sensing functions, retaining breathability and directional moisture transport. Notably, the polyelectrolyte membrane‐enhanced fabric achieves 9.86°C sub‐ambient cooling (101 W m − 2 net cooling power) under 1 sun intensity, 100% accurate motion monitoring, and stable triboelectric output (10 V stable output under 10 N constant force), along with exceptional durability (1000 folding cycles), recyclability, and antibacterial activity. Owing to the prominent advantages of structural innovation, excellent performance, and strong practicality, this study can not only be effectively extended to other inorganic particle systems (e.g., SiO 2 , boron nitride) but also holds broad application prospects in wearable electronic devices, flexible robots, and intelligent sensing systems.

title_zh: Morphology‐Controlled Silica Nanoparticle Coatings for Transparent Radiative Cooling
title_en: Morphology‐Controlled Silica Nanoparticle Coatings for Transparent Radiative Cooling
authors_short: Jefferson An Sien Lam；Kishin Matsumori；Maximillian Theis 等
abstract_en: ABSTRACT In this study, transparent passive radiative cooling coatings are introduced by immobilizing solid and hollow silica (SiO 2 ) spheres on glass substrates. It is showcased that particle morphology within a sub‐monolayer coating strongly influences visible and atmospheric window reflectance of glass. Solid and hollow‐sphere particles of total diameter within the Mie regime reduce atmospheric window reflectance ( R AW ) at the expense of higher visible reflectance ( R VIS ). This trade‐off is dependent on particle and core diameter. Solid particles with particle diameter >1000 nm can reduce the R AW of glass by up to 65 %, though increase R VIS by 25 %. Meanwhile, the use of hollow‐sphere nanoparticles of similar diameters and thin shells (25–50 nm) can reduce the R AW of glass by up to 35 % with minimal changes to R VIS . These spectroscopic trends are validated numerically via both Mie theory and effective medium theory. The work demonstrates that hollow‐sphere morphology is a valuable lever to control passive radiative cooling for various solar applications requiring transparency, such as coatings for windows or photovoltaic devices.

title_zh: Transparent Metamaterial Films with Multimodal Radiative Cooling for Outdoor Flexible Electronic Devices
title_en: Transparent Metamaterial Films with Multimodal Radiative Cooling for Outdoor Flexible Electronic Devices
abstract_en: Effective thermal management presents a critical challenge for next-generation, high-power, flexible electronics, requiring innovative and energy-efficient strategies to safeguard device reliability and performance. Passive radiative cooling, a zero-energy carbon-free solution, has emerged as a highly promising approach. However, integrating heat conduction, radiation, and convection into a unified thermal management system for electronic displays without compromising optical transparency remains challenging. Here, we design a multimodal transparent radiative cooling film fabricated by embedding diamond microparticles into a poly(dimethylsiloxane) elastomer matrix and patterning its surface with a pyramidal micronano array (PDMS/D-PA). The optimized film exhibits high solar spectral transmittance of 81.8%, broadband mid-infrared emissivity of 98%, and enhanced thermal conductivity of 3.33 W m –1 K –1 . Outdoor tests show that the film-coated device achieves a steady-state temperature reduction of 14.8 °C compared to a bare counterpart under a solar irradiance of 820.8 W m –2 . An alkylation treatment further renders the film superhydrophobicity with a water contact angle of 153.4°, providing self-cleaning capability and environmental durability. This composite film bridges the gap between esthetic needs and functional demands, offering a sustainable, passive thermal management strategy for ensuring the reliability and longevity of flexible outdoor electronic devices, such as wearable sensors, foldable displays, e-skin, and drone components.

abstract_en: Passive radiative cooling (PRC) shows potential for energy savings, especially in the construction and transportation industries. However, it is prone to efficiency loss due to influences from the environment. To address this challenge, we constructed a ZnAl layered double oxide (ZnAl-LDO) substrate, which has optical selectivity, and modified it with a cross-linked surfactant of SiO 2 /PFDTES, finally yielding an advanced ZnAl-LDO M2 coating material with PRC performance and enhanced environmental durability. According to the tests, the solar reflectivity and thermal emissivity of the prepared ZnAl-LDO M2 coating can reach 99% and 98%, respectively, after being calcined at 500 °C for 4 h. In addition, the contact and slide angles for water and oil on the coating can be improved to 160.2°/5.4° and 141°/12.9°, respectively, demonstrating the amphiphobicity of the product. In an outdoor test, the obtained coating can reduce the temperature by up to 12.6 °C. Furthermore, the simulation results show that 29.82% of cooling energy expenditure can be saved if the coating is applied to the surface of the building. Moreover, the coating exhibits environmental tolerance abilities, such as resistance to acid and alkali corrosions. These data indicate that the as-prepared ZnAl-LDO M2 coating has promising prospects in the field of eco-friendly refrigeration.

Rising cooling demands motivate passive alternatives to air conditioning. This study evaluates a transparent skylight window for daytime passive radiative cooling (PRC) under outdoor summer conditions in Turku, Finland. The inserts (Ø 0.10 m) were positioned diagonally in the lower window facing indoors and in the upper window facing the sky. The upper SWG carried a 3 M solar-control thin film (TF, ∼65% solar reflectance). The sky facing CG surfaces were covered with dispersed TiO 2 –SiO 2 nanoparticles (NPs, ≈30% areal coverage). The skylight gas volume contained air, CO 2 , or air/NH 3 (2:1). A pyrgeometer provided local weather data as long-wave (LW) irradiance (L↓).
